Good afternoon, private banking, Rachel Tan speaking. How may I help you today?

Hi Rachel, Adrian Lim here. Calling about my existing holding. Office quite noisy today, so I've stepped into the meeting room. Got a gap between business calls, and I want to get my personal administration out of the way lah.

Certainly, Mr Lim. Are you comfortable speaking there, or would you prefer to call back from somewhere more private?

Can, door closed already. Nobody else in here. I've got the account page open on my phone, although the screen quite small. My NRIC is S double six two five double two one A. My date of birth is 24 November 1983.

Thank you. We can keep the conversation focused. When you receive your portfolio summaries, is the current layout convenient to read on your phone?

The headings okay, but the commentary very long leh. Prefer the main points at the front, then I can read the rest when the office quiet. Otherwise I keep scrolling while people are waiting for me.

I can note your preference for concise summaries with the main points presented first. What would you like to discuss about your holding today?

Let me get to it before the phone starts ringing again ah. Got my account page in front of me. The recent weakness looks like a chance to add, so please buy 1,000 units of Crest Emerging Markets Bond Fund using a market order, for a transaction amount of 750,000 renminbi.

I have heard what you have said. Take your time if there is anything else you want to raise before we continue.

Wait wait, cancel that earlier instruction before anything gets executed. My business may need the cash, so better reduce the holding instead. Aiyoh, too many things on my mind today. Better I stop trying to answer office messages while talking to you.

I understand your objective is to reduce emerging-market credit exposure and make your portfolio more liquid for potential business needs.

For these calls, better keep the wording direct lah. My office conversations jump from topic to topic already; with personal administration I prefer to finish the discussion properly, without all the extra commentary.

I will keep my wording direct. I recommend reducing your holding in Crest Emerging Markets Bond Fund because that lowers your exposure to emerging-market credit and liquidity risks, supporting your aim of freeing up cash for business needs.

Hmm, let me sit with that for a moment. Got messages flashing on the screen again, but those can wait. Carrying on with the call easier than switching back and forth.

With Crest Emerging Markets Bond Fund, deteriorating credit quality or defaults by the bond issuers can reduce the value of the fund's holdings. During emerging-market stress, those bonds may also become harder to trade, putting further pressure on the fund's value. You could lose some or all of the capital you have invested in this fund. Do you understand how issuer defaults and difficulty trading the underlying bonds could reduce the fund's value?

Yes, I understand. If the issuers cannot pay, or the bonds become hard to trade, the fund's value can drop. Please keep the rest brief ah. No need to rush your words, just leave out the extra commentary. Easier for me to follow like that.

The transaction fee is 0.3% of the transaction value.

My screen went dark already. Give me a moment to bring it back. The quantity, let me check my screen, I want to put— Let me start again: please sell 1,000 units of Crest Emerging Markets Bond Fund using a limit order, with a minimum sale price of 750 renminbi per unit. The transaction amount is 750,000 renminbi instead.

Your replacement instruction is to sell 1,000 units of Crest Emerging Markets Bond Fund using a limit order, with a transaction amount of 750,000 renminbi and a minimum sale price of 750 renminbi per unit. Please explicitly confirm whether this is your final instruction.

Mm, let me think a bit first ah. Got a business message coming in.

I will give you some space. If you need to end the call to deal with your business message, you can contact me again when you are available.

Need to take this one now. I'll get back to you when the office settles down. Thanks Rachel, sorry for the interruption ah.

Thank you for calling, Mr Lim. Goodbye.
